title: Typed Payload Gateway: fallback semantics and constrained-decoder probe for streaming structured outputs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In streaming + tool-calling flows we observe intermittent constrained-decoder failures and partial payloads that fail schema validation. Current test harnesses detect failures but do not exercise realistic fallback transformations used by Console/runtime. Goal: Implement a 'Typed Payload Gateway' test layer that simulates production fallback sanitizers (type coercion, missing-field synthesis, sentinel insertion) and run a cross-model constrained-decoder probe to measure how often fallbacks are needed and whether the sanitizers preserve intent and downstream tool-calling correctness. Deliverables: 1) a small runtime-adjacent gateway harness that can sit between streaming output and schema enforcer, 2) a suite of randomized probing scenarios (stream interruptions, token drop, interleaved toolcall markers), 3) acceptance criteria and telemetry hooks to detect regressions and quantify repair success rate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gateway can accept partial streaming events and apply at least 3 sanitization strategies (type normalization, default-field injection, trailing-sentinel trimming) and return a validated payload to downstream contract enforcer. 2) Probe harness runs across 5 model variants and produces reproducible per-scenario metrics (repair-rate, false-positive repairs, latency cost). 3) No user-visible behavior regression for >=95% of canonical prompt set in console e2e. 4) Tests are integrated into CI and a dashboard shows weekly regression alerts.
test_plan: Unit tests for each sanitizer rule (coercion, defaulting, sentinel-trim)
Integration test: streaming emulator -> gateway -> constrained-decoder -> schema-enforcer with injected token-drop faults
Cross-model probe: run randomized interruptions against models: redwood-mini-v1, redwood-compat-v2, openllm-3b, opt-13b, and a quantized 7B variant
Chaos schedule: simulate network chunk boundaries where partial JSON fragments are emitted and verify gateway recovers consistent payloads
Performance test: measure additional mean-latency introduced by gateway at 50/200/500 RPS
metrics: repair_rate: percent of failed streams that gateway converts to schema-compliant payloads
false_repair_rate: percent of converted payloads that change semantics (measured by golden prompts)
implementation_notes: Prefer a small Python harness that mirrors production sanitizer rules. Keep gateway stateless and deterministic for reproducibility. Expose a debug mode that emits pre/post payload diffs and attaches a confidence tag for each sanitization. Instrument with telemetry tags: model_family, stream_interruption_type, sanitizer_strategy. Add unit tests that fuzz partial-stream boundaries and verify idempotence of repeated sanitization.
risks: Over-aggressive sanitization that masks model regressions and hides root causes
Latency overhead from gateway in high-throughput paths
False-positive repairs that alter user intent and misroute tool calls
rollback_plan: If we observe >5% false_repair_rate on the canonical prompt set during staging, revert sanitizer rules incrementally and keep only non-destructive strategies (trailing-sentinel-trim) until root cause analysis completes.
